messages.subject: Re: Where to report issues ... ???
messages.body_plain:
I was asked below, back in June, as to the best place for feature requests for Rattle.

A new web site, http://connect-r.com, is looking like a pretty good place to manage feature requests (and not just for Rattle but also for R). It is in the early stages of development but already is useful. I've responded there to one Rattle feature request so far (now implemented in the latest release of Rattle). Feel free to add feature requests there - and use it as the central place which I will be monitoring. It also opens up the opportunity for others to contribute toward the request.

Even if you don't have a feature request it is useful to see which requests are most popular and hence perhaps more likely to be implemented (the request I resolved happened to be the most voted for request on the site so far!). So login and vote for a useful feature.

It seems early days for ConnectR but I will be adding a few of my own To Do items there to gauge interest in them.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Starting Rattle Every Time
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I installed R version 3.1.1 and the all necessary files for Rattle 3.0 Wednesday 8/20/2014 and played around with Rattle to test drive it.  Everything was  ok so I ordered the Rattle book from Amazon.com to learn Rattle better.  But the following day when I opened R and tried to run Rattle by typing > library(rattle) I got the message: Error in library(rattle) : there is no package called 'rattle'.  I even enclosed rattle in double quotes to see if that was the problem and still got the same error message.  This is my first time of using Rattle. Having earlier installed "RGtk2" I don't think I need to install it again on my Windows 7 machine each time I want to start Rattle.

So what am I doing wrong, and what different procedure should I follow every time I want to start Rattle?  I will appreciate any help, please.  Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Starting Rattle Every Time
messages.body_plain:
That's an odd problem - you certainly should not have to install packages multiple times.

Perhaps try installing rattle again:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source")

then reboot and ensure it is still available. If not, there must be some system configuration issue?

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

CK

messages.subject: histogram appears as screen junk
messages.body_plain:
In have installed rattle on Ubuntu 12.04 w/R 3.1.1

I followed all the directions on
http://rattle.togaware.com/rattle-install-ubuntu.html

in particular, all the packages are installed without error (that took some doing!)

Under the Explore tab, I can successfully execute Box Plot, Cumulative, and Benford.

Histogram fails because the plot windows is filled with screen junk, parts of whatever happens to be on my desktop.
In the terminal appears the message: Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'p' not found

The relevant part of the Log file follows.  Please help.

Regards,

Bruce

#============================================================
# Rattle timestamp: 2014-08-24 14:37:22 x86_64-pc-linux-gnu

# Histogram Plots

# The 'ggplot2' package provides the 'ggplot' function.

require(ggplot2, quietly=TRUE)

# The 'dplyr' package provides the 'select' function.

require(dplyr, quietly=TRUE)

# Histogram Plot for cohort_dom_filer

ar <- range(with(crs, select(dataset[sample,], cohort_dom_filer)))
bw <- (ar[2]-ar[1])/nclass.FD(with(crs, dataset[sample,]$cohort_dom_filer))

p <- p + geom_histogram(aes(y=..density..), binwidth=bw, fill="grey", colour="black")
p <- p + geom_density()

p <- p + xlab("cohort_dom_filer\n\nRattle 2014-Aug-24 14:37:22 bdm25")
p <- p + ggtitle("Distribution of cohort_dom_filer (sample)")
p <- p + labs(colour="") + xlab("Density")
print(p)
